en: Air is not empty space; it is a mixture of gases like nitrogen and oxygen that has mass and takes up physical space.
Melting solid ice into liquid water is a physical change because the H2O molecules remain exactly the same, just moving more freely.
Mixing sand in water creates a suspension, not a true solution, because the solid sand particles will eventually settle at the bottom.
Helium gas inside a party balloon has measurable mass and weight, which is why a filled balloon is heavier than a completely empty one.
The bubbles in boiling water contain water vapor, making boiling a physical change of state rather than a chemical reaction that creates new gases.
Rusting is a chemical change where solid iron reacts with oxygen and moisture to form a completely new, flaky substance called iron oxide.
Puddles dry up because liquid water evaporates into invisible water vapor at room temperature, long before it ever reaches its boiling point.
Sugar does not truly disappear when dissolved in tea; its molecules simply spread out evenly among the water molecules, keeping the drink sweet.
Solid metal bridges expand and increase in length during hot summer days, proving that solids, not just liquids and gases, expand when heated.
Burning a wooden log is a chemical change that destroys the original wood to create entirely new substances like ash, smoke, and carbon dioxide.
Not all metals are magnetic, because common metallic materials like aluminum foil and copper wire will not stick to a refrigerator magnet.
The white mist above a kettle is liquid water droplets, whereas actual water vapor is a completely invisible gas you cannot see.
